syntax: ${PARAMETER_NAME@LOCALIZED_STRING_SS} — one parameter per visible string, alone in its element. Each element also carries data-copy="<slot>", the wave-18 convention.
rules: CMS owns copy only. No parameter here is, contains, defaults, mirrors or logs a protected runtime value.
No vertical, tenant or business copy is hardcoded in the source — no Calm Harbor, no Beauty, no English-only string.
Example copy below is SAFE FILLER for review and for the evidence harness. It is not a product decision and must be re-authored per locale before activation.
Error copy is non-enumerating: it never says why verification failed beyond the supplied string, never counts attempts and never hints at lockout.
AUTH_BRAND_NAME and AUTH_PITCH_EYEBROW are the SAME parameters the wave-18 login page uses. Registering them once serves both pages.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_DOCUMENT_TITLE
parameters.notes: No brand concatenation in markup — a locale that wants the brand in the title puts it in this string.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_SUBTITLE
parameters.example: Enter the code from your authenticator app to finish signing in.
parameters.notes: True in all four states — it must not describe enrollment, which is state-dependent.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_SETUP
parameters.example: Set up your authenticator app. Scan this code with the app you use for verification codes, then enter the code it shows.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_QR_ALT
parameters.example: Setup code for your authenticator app. If you cannot scan it, use the setup key below.
parameters.notes: Must point at the manual key, because the image is useless to anyone who cannot scan or see it.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_SECRET_LABEL
parameters.notes: Names the {{TWO_FACTOR_SECRET}} value that follows it in reading order.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_SECRET_HINT
parameters.example: Cannot scan? Enter this key in your authenticator app instead. Spaces and letter case do not matter.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_NOTICE
parameters.example: Your authenticator app is already set up. Open it to get your current code.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_CODE_LABEL
parameters.notes: Always present. The label is explicit and visible in all four states.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_CODE_HINT
parameters.example: Six digits, from your authenticator app.
parameters.notes: Accessible description, named by the input's aria-describedby. Digit count lives in copy, not in a pattern attribute — the server stays the only validator.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_ERROR
parameters.example: That code did not work. Open your authenticator app for a new code and try again.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_BUTTON
parameters.notes: One action, one label, all four states. No second label for a loading or disabled state — neither exists.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_NOTE
parameters.example: Codes are generated on your device. We will never ask you for one by email, message or phone.
parameters.notes: The optional security/help note. Anti-phishing counterpart of the login note.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_PITCH_TITLE
parameters.example: One more step before you’re in.
parameters.notes: Step-specific, NOT shared with login: login's pitch asserts that a password is entered on that page, which is false here.

parameters.name: TWO_FACTOR_PITCH_BODY
parameters.example: This second step runs on the account service, not in the portal. Once your code is confirmed, you’ll be taken straight back to where you started.
parameters.notes: Step-specific, same reason. Keeps the anti-phishing framing of the login pitch.

runtimePlaceholders.owner: core-auth — supplied per request. CMS creates no parameter, default, fixture, log, analytics attribute or JavaScript variable for any of these, and every one survives the CMS-rendered HTML byte-for-byte until substitution.
referenced: {{TWO_FACTOR_QR_CODE}} — QR image src, a core-auth data URL
{{TWO_FACTOR_SECRET}} — generated setup key, rendered as text
notReferenced: {{TWO_FACTOR_OTPAUTH_URI}} — deliberately unreferenced: no visible control needs it in this brief, and an unused placeholder is one more protected value on the page. Adding it later is a markup-only change.
